title: Chapter 18: The binomial theorem and Pascal’s triangle

questions.stem:
By using the fact that \((1+x)^{11}=(1+x)^3(1+x)^8\). Show that

\(\binom{11}{5}=\binom85+\binom31\binom84+\binom32\binom83+\binom82\)
questions.hint: Equate the coefficient of x⁵ on both sides.

steps.explain: Compare the coefficient of \(x^5\) on both sides. On the left, by the binomial theorem:
On the right, write both expansions.
An \(x^5\) term comes from \(x^j\) in the first times \(x^{5-j}\) in the second, for \(j=0,1,2,3\).

questions.answer: Coefficient of x⁵ on the left: \(\binom{11}{5}\). On the right, x⁵ arises from x^j (from (1+x)³) times x^{5−j} (from (1+x)⁸), j = 0…3: \(\binom30\binom85+\binom31\binom84+\binom32\binom83+\binom33\binom82\). Since \(\binom30=\binom33=1\), equating gives the result.

keyPoints.note: Find the x⁵ coefficient on each side of (1 + x)¹¹ = (1 + x)³(1 + x)⁸.
